collection.credit:
* V10 reputation, appointment, school and rivalry events: event prose
  and detailed branching by ChatGPT. Requested social outcomes and
  leadership roles, including ostracism, laughingstock, village idiot,
  mad scientist, trusted advisor, teacher and heads of professions:
  Lorsieab2. VV3–VV5-only Magic/Nature faction rule: Lorsieab2.

items.text: ruining a festival centerpiece with slug slime
pulverizing someone else's polished pearls for paint
stealing a pouch of gemstones
replacing good timber with rotten wood
contaminating a display with cave guano
secretly sabotaging a rival's sculpture
lying about who invented the new snail-shell plaster
mocking a child's carefully made gift
Nobody sits beside (Subject) at the feast. An elderly villager moves over and says, "There's room here."
Children repeat the accusation as a cruel rhyme. Their teacher intervenes and explains why it is wrong.
A friend leaves a meal at (Subject)'s door but is too frightened to stay. (Subject) feels grateful and hurt.
(Subject) begins to believe the rumors. A healer reminds (subject.him/her) that public opinion is not evidence.
The leaders formally end the exclusion and invite (Subject) back, acknowledging that trust may take time.
The rivals continue to hate each other's guts, but agree not to interfere with each other's work.
One says, "I don't forgive you." The other replies, "I didn't ask you to. I asked you to stop lying."
They work together during an emergency, then resume avoiding each other afterward.
The leaders require a neutral witness whenever the two share materials until the dispute is resolved.
(Subject) becomes a respected advocate for fair hearings.
(Subject) remains unpopular, but is no longer excluded.
A former accuser asks for advice; (Subject) chooses whether to help.
The villagers remember the scandal long after the truth is established. (Subject) learns to live with the discomfort without pretending it is fair.
A child publicly says, "You were right." It means more than the council's entire speech.
The confessor must publicly correct the story and help repair the damage.
The confessor is embarrassed by the attention and learns to ask questions before assuming guilt.
The confession itself becomes a village joke; a teacher stops the teasing when it turns cruel.
The confessor explains why (confessor.he/she) was frightened. The adults listen rather than treating the lie as a joke.
Restitution is accepted, but forgiveness is not immediate.
The wrongdoer becomes a temporary laughingstock, then slowly earns trust by doing ordinary reliable work.
The wrongdoer refuses to improve and is excluded from managing shared supplies for a while.
An apprentice says, "You taught me better than this." That hurts more than the formal penalty.

intro.name: The accusation
intro.text: A villager named (Subject) is accused of {A}. By sunset, nearly everyone knows the story. Unfortunately, nearly everyone knows a DIFFERENT version of it.

question.name: Two sides
question.text: (Subject) is {furious and defiant|ashamed and silent|bewildered by the accusation|too proud to ask for help}. (Friend), the accuser, is {genuinely convinced|jealous|repeating a rumor|covering up (friend.his/her) own mistake}.

choices.label: HOLD A FAIR HEARING BEFORE IMPOSING PENALTIES.
ASK BOTH SIDES TO PRODUCE EVIDENCE.
LET THE VILLAGE COUNCIL IMPOSE A SHORT COOLING-OFF PERIOD.
ASK A TRUSTED ELDER TO MEDIATE.

h2.text: An apprentice produces a labeled jar proving the material was borrowed with permission.

h3.text: (Subject) angrily insults the council. The hearing continues; rudeness is not proof of guilt.

v1.text: The supposed stolen pearls are found inside a hollow coconut.

v2.text: A smear of slug slime implicates the wrong person because three villagers used the same tool.

v3.text: A written confession appears, but the handwriting belongs to someone else.

v4.text: The evidence shows (Subject) knowingly sabotaged the work.

cooling.text: The leaders ask the disputants to avoid each other for two days, without cutting anyone off from food, shelter, healthcare, or family.

text_only.reason: a promise that nothing is taken away; no food or health changes

k1.text: The pause prevents a fight, but rumors worsen.

k2.text: (Subject) feels ostracised and begins to withdraw.

k3.text: (Friend) realizes the punishment was premature and asks for the case to be reopened.

d2.text: The elder is biased toward (Friend). A second, neutral mediator is appointed.

d3.text: The two agree on what happened but not what it meant.

proof.text: The council announces that suspicion is not a verdict.

pr1.text: Some villagers apologize. Others continue whispering.

pr2.text: A child asks why everyone believed the worst so quickly.

pr3.text: The accuser becomes furious and refuses to accept the finding.

exon.text: (Subject) is cleared. The leaders correct the public record.
exon.name: Exoneration

x1.text: The village celebrates the discovery, but (Subject) does not feel ready to celebrate with them.

x2.text: (Friend) admits the mistake and apologizes without excuses.

false.text: A third villager admits writing the confession.

fc2.text: (confessor.He/She) wanted attention and did not expect the rumor to become serious.

fc3.text: (confessor.He/She) genuinely believed (confessor.he/she) was responsible, having confused two similar jars.

wrong.text: (Subject) admits the sabotage after the evidence is presented.

wd1.text: (subject.He/She) repairs the damage and loses the competition prize.

wd2.text: (subject.He/She) is suspended from judging future contests for a time.

wd3.text: (subject.He/She) refuses to apologize. The community maintains proportionate boundaries.
